name: Phu Quoc food guide
summary: Bún quây is the morning bowl: rice-flour noodles, seafood, and a sauce you mix. Dinner is boiled crab at Hàm Ninh, gỏi cá trích in rice paper, and the catch at the night market. Fish sauce and pepper are what you carry home.
body: Start the day with bún quây, the island’s stirred noodle bowl: rice-flour noodles, fish, shrimp, and squid, with a dip of chili, sugar, fish sauce, and citrus you mix yourself. It came from central Vietnam in 1955 as a ground-shrimp bowl called bún tôm, took on the island’s seafood in 1996, and now runs from morning into the evening on the street across from the Dương Đông harbour and along Long Beach.

Dinner comes from the sea. Grilled nhum scooped up with lime and pepper, gỏi cá trích rolled in rice paper, crab boiled at Hàm Ninh, sweet tôm mũ ni, sea snails, grilled cobia, and cá sòng off the charcoal. Away from the water there is bún kèn in a coconut-and-curry broth, honey coffee at a bee farm, and stream fish, sim wine, and grilled biên mai seed on the park walk.

Fish sauce and pepper are what you carry home. Nước mắm Phú Quốc ages in wooden vats. Nitrogen is 20–43 gN/lít, and up to 40°N. Output is over 10 million litres a year, and also about 6 million, at trên 25ºC. The anchovy is placed in the Gulf of Thailand, and also in the clear Andaman Sea. The pepper gardens send out over 1,000 tons a year.
specialtiesLead: Bún quây, nước mắm, and hồ tiêu come first, then the seafood plates, the park snacks, and the meals on the northern sand.

sections.heading: Bowls and seafood
paragraphs: The bowls and plates the island cooks from its own water: noodles in the morning, grilled and boiled seafood after dark.

spots.name: Bun quay
spots.address: Dương Đông harbour street, and Long Beach
spots.note: Rice-flour noodles in a stirred broth with fish, shrimp, squid, herbs, and onion, eaten with a dip you mix from chili, sugar, fish sauce, and citrus. It is a morning bowl by tradition, served now into the evening.

spots.name: Bun ken
spots.note: A noodle bowl with Cambodian roots, in a broth of dried fish, coconut milk, and a dash of curry powder.

spots.name: Goi ca trich
spots.note: Raw herring with mint, onion, shredded coconut, and crisp vegetables, rolled in rice paper and dipped in fish sauce with garlic, chili, and roasted peanuts. It tastes aromatic and fresh, a salad for a hot day.

spots.name: Ghe Ham Ninh
spots.note: Crab boiled as soon as it comes off the boat, red-shelled with firm, fragrant meat, dipped in salt, pepper, and lime. The smaller crabs carry more flavour.

spots.name: Nhum bien
spots.note: Sea urchin grilled with oil, roasted peanuts, and spring onion until creamy, then scooped out and dipped in lime and pepper. Zest, spice, and a fresh sea aroma.

spots.name: Grilled oysters
spots.note: Oysters grilled in the shell and served with sea urchin, roasted shallots, peanuts, and green onion.

spots.name: Ca song nuong
spots.note: Horse mackerel grilled on charcoal with salt and chili, then wrapped in rice paper with herbs and vegetables. Aromatic and sweet, meatier and less fishy than most seafood.

spots.name: Tom mu ni
spots.note: Clawless slipper lobster boiled until tender, with sweet white tail meat between shrimp and lobster. Dip it in lime, salt, and Phú Quốc pepper.

spots.name: Oc
spots.note: Sea snails, plentiful and inexpensive and served in many kinds. Watch what the next table is eating, then order more than one.

spots.name: Grilled cobia
spots.note: Cobia grilled as a seafood plate, eaten with sea urchin and herring salad as the taste of the island.

spots.name: Squid
spots.address: Dinh Cau night market, or back on shore after a night catch
spots.note: One of the island’s most popular seafood plates, best eaten back on shore after a night squid-fishing trip. The night market sells it too.

spots.name: Ca suoi
spots.note: Fish from the park’s streams, Suối Tranh, suối Đá Bàn, and suối Đá Ngọn, eaten on the forest walk with sim wine and grilled biên mai seed.

sections.heading: Pantry, drinks, and snacks
paragraphs: Fish sauce, pepper, and sim wine are what the island sends you home with, and cashews and dried seaweed sit on the same night-market tables. Bãi Thơm adds a coconut, a hotpot, and a seafood platter on the sand.

spots.name: Nuoc mam Phu Quoc
spots.address: Barrel houses along the old Dương Đông river
spots.note: Anchovy fish sauce aged in wooden vats, dark as a cockroach wing, salty and deeply sweet with a natural fat. It smells light and clean, with no fishy edge.

spots.name: Ho tieu
spots.note: Peppercorns from the island’s gardens, aromatic and spicy, with a floral nose and real heat. Taste them on a morning garden visit and take a bag home.

spots.name: Ruou sim
spots.address: Bãi Sao, the national park, and the Dinh Cau night market
spots.note: A wine made from forest sim fruit, sold on the island as myrtle wine. Pour a glass at Bãi Sao or after the forest walk.

spots.name: Cui bien mai nuong
spots.address: Bãi Sao and the national park
spots.note: A local seed grilled over the fire, the snack after a swim at Bãi Sao or on the park walk.

spots.name: Honey coffee
spots.note: Coffee and sweets made with island honey, tasted while you walk among the hives.

spots.name: Cashew nuts
spots.note: Cashew nuts, one of the things the island is known for, sold beside the fish sauce and pepper to carry home.

spots.name: Dried seaweed
spots.note: Dried seaweed, one of the island’s take-home foods, sold beside the fish sauce and pepper.

spots.name: Coconut
spots.note: A coconut on the sand, the drink of the northern beach stop.

spots.name: Beach hotpot
spots.note: A hotpot shared on the beach, the sit-down meal of the northern stop.

spots.name: Seafood platter
spots.note: A seafood platter eaten on the sand, ordered with a coconut or a hotpot.

sections.heading: International dining
paragraphs: Western food is served along Bãi Sao and Long Beach. High-end beachfront rooms offer Japanese-French fusion and grilled beef.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: Dinner is the night market in Dương Đông. Three wordings sit side by side: 50-plus stalls on a pedestrian Bạch Đằng, 100-odd stalls near Dinh Cậu with the streets closed to traffic from 5 pm until midnight, and more than a hundred vendors. Each is listed below.

spots.name: Dinh Cau night market
spots.note: The streets near the rock temple close to traffic from 5 pm until midnight, and more than half of the 100-odd stalls sell food.

spots.name: Phu Quoc Night Market
spots.note: A pedestrian street in the evening, with 50-plus stalls of seafood and local dishes.

spots.name: Duong Dong seafood market
spots.note: Choose from the day’s catch and have it grilled, boiled, steamed, or stir-fried at the stall.

spots.name: Rach Vem
spots.note: Floating restaurants on the beach beside Starfish Beach, where you lie in a hammock and eat seafood cooked from the water in front of you. One itinerary puts the fishing village about 20 km north of Duong Dong.

spots.name: Long Beach
spots.note: Food, drink, and cocktails along the sand from sunset into the evening, on white tablecloths or plastic stools, with Western menus beside the Vietnamese ones.

spots.name: Sao Beach
spots.note: Western and Vietnamese food along the beach, plus grilled biên mai seed and sim wine. One itinerary lists entrance and parking as free.

spots.name: Bai Thom
spots.note: A coconut, a hotpot, or a seafood platter on the northern sand.

spots.name: Ham Ninh
spots.address: About 20 km northeast of Dương Đông
spots.note: Crab boiled straight off the boat and dipped in salt, pepper, and lime, in a fishing village where the crab is in almost all year.

sections.heading: Fine dining
paragraphs: The island serves fine-dining meals, many hotels plate gourmet food beside the sea, and a barbecue can be set on the sand. High-end beachfront rooms round out the evening.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Bún quây is the island breakfast by tradition: rice-flour noodles, seafood, and a sauce you mix. It is now served through the day and into the evening too.

seoTitle: Phu Quoc food guide — bun quay, fish sauce, and the night market
seoDescription: Bún quây in the morning, boiled crab at Hàm Ninh, grilled sea urchin at the Dinh Cậu night market, and fish sauce and pepper to carry home: 22 Phu Quoc specialties.
